interpreted_intent: Create one independent, complex, photographically plausible Stonepunk concept for later image generation and rendered-pixel testing, using the supplied portrait strictly as an appearance-only reference for one clearly adult subject. For this arm, Stonepunk is an agent interpretation of a speculative technological culture whose working mechanisms, architecture, clothing hardware, and energy-reading system are visibly built from carved stone and integrated minerals rather than a requester-supplied definition.
subject: One unmistakably adult woman whose facial appearance and hair follow the supplied portrait as appearance-only reference material, recast as a stone-mechanism tide keeper in wholly new clothing and surroundings.
setting: A wind-beaten tidal observatory formed from fitted concentric basalt rings above a rough sea at blue hour.
event: The woman seats a quartz chronometer into a hand-cranked stone astrolabe and turns its granite crank, transmitting motion through the observatory until an outer monolith ring aligns with an incoming wave.
visual_priorities: mechanically legible, interconnected technology made predominantly from basalt, granite, shale, and quartz
a readable two-hand activation event with an already-visible architectural consequence
appearance-only continuity with the supplied adult portrait while wardrobe, role, action, and environment are newly authored
baseline_prompt_en: A cinematic Stonepunk environmental portrait inside a tidal observatory carved from colossal concentric basalt rings. An unmistakably adult woman, using the supplied portrait only for facial appearance, has long near-black wavy hair, warm brown almond-shaped eyes, softly arched brows, a slim oval face, and natural rose lips. She wears a black woven-flax mantle armored with overlapping polished-shale plates and stone fasteners. At blue hour she locks a fist-sized quartz chronometer into a hand-cranked stone astrolabe. Her left hand braces the crystal socket while her right turns a carved granite crank. Interlocking basalt gears, counterweighted monolith arms, and grooved circular tracks visibly transmit the motion: one outer ring has shifted open toward a breaking wave. Veins of quartz embedded through the mechanism glow and trace measured tide lines across raised carvings. Salt spray catches the mineral light; wet stone, wind-tossed hair, and precise hand contact ground the scene as physically photographed working technology.
